# Approvals + replay

<!-- Generated by `go run docs/roadmap/gen.go docs` from tickets.json. Do not edit by hand. -->

**Phase:** [P2 · Proven identity](../README.md#phase-2--proven-identity) · **Lane:** Control plane · **Label:** `feature:policy-approvals` · **Epic:** [#100](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/100) · **Tickets:** 9 (2S 7M)

Every change that would widen what agents can reach, or where real credentials are sent, is held as a draft until a second person approves it. Before approving, the reviewer sees the structural diff, the reasons the change counts as widening, and a replay of recent fleet traffic that compares base and draft decisions. Narrowing changes still apply at once. The feature is off by default and needs OIDC console auth, the versioned policy store and admin audit.

## How we build it

- Config and back-compat: a new CP-local `console.approvals` block in the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig (`json:"-"`, read only from the operator `--config` through `config.LoadConsole`, never from the served config.yaml, policyWire or SettingsWire), so a settings save can never turn the gate off. Keys and defaults: enabled false, minApprovals 1 (1..3), allowSelfApproveNarrowing true, allowEmergencyApply false, replayWindow 168h (1h..720h), replayMaxEvents 100000 (max 100000), replayTimeout 60s, replayMaxAge 24h, draftTTL 168h, maxOpenDrafts 200. A change needs a CP restart. When enabled, startup fails with an error naming the missing prerequisite unless console.auth=oidc, `--policy-store=versioned` (W-P1-PVER-01), `--state-dir` and `console.adminAudit.enabled=true` (W-P1-AAUD-01) are all set. When disabled, no approvals migration runs and every P1 endpoint, status code and /policy byte is unchanged.
- One chokepoint: W-P2-APPR-06 changes the W-P1-PVER-02 `Server.publish` to take an `approvals.Clearance`, a type with unexported fields that only `approvals.Gate` can mint, and publish rejects the zero value. The Gate returns a Clearance when approvals are disabled, for a narrowing change when allowSelfApproveNarrowing is true, for an applied draft, for the `system:import` first-start migration, and for a break-glass emergency apply. Otherwise it returns ErrApprovalRequired. WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteLLMProviders, the W-P1-PVER-03 rollback route and the W-P1-PVER-06 `warden policy import` CLI all go through it, so a new publish caller that skips the gate does not compile. External YAML edits stay unserved per W-P1-PVER-05.
- Data model (cpstate migration `approvals/0001`, applied only when enabled): `change_drafts(id, target policy|blocked_users|agents, target_ref, revision, base_version, state, author_iss, author_sub, author_email, author_kind, source console|rollback|cli|api|git|admin-mcp, provenance_json, message, doc_json, doc_sha256, classification_json, required_role, last_error, created_at, updated_at, expires_at, applied_version)` and append-only `change_approvals(id, draft_id, revision, doc_sha256, approver_iss, approver_sub, approver_email, approver_role, auth_method, decision approve|reject|self|emergency|post_review, replay_id, acknowledge_no_replay, comment, at)`. For the policy target, doc_json is the same redacted canonical doc (allowlist, denylist, settings) that `policy_versions.doc_json` stores, with secretAccessKey replaced by its `sha256:<16 hex>` fingerprint and blockedUsers excluded. YAML is never stored. `source` and `provenance_json` exist now so p4-gitops and p4-admin-mcp need no migration. The `approvals.Store` interface has a SQLite implementation so p5-postgres-ha can add its own.
- State machine in internal/approvals, one compare-and-swap transaction per transition (`UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND state=? AND revision=?`): draft -> pending (submit); pending -> applied | rejected | needs_rebase; draft | pending | needs_rebase -> withdrawn (author) or expired (sweeper, after draftTTL); needs_rebase -> pending (rebase); pending | needs_rebase -> applied_unreviewed (emergency apply) -> applied (post-hoc review). An edit (PUT) or rebase creates revision n+1, voids earlier approvals and replays, and re-classifies. Each approval row records revision and doc_sha256. When the last required approval for the current revision arrives, the same request re-runs Classify against the live head and publishes with expectedHead=base_version through the publish path, which reruns the full NewLocalYAMLProvider validation. A 422 leaves the draft pending with last_error. An ErrConflict moves it to needs_rebase. Rebase applies the W-P1-PVER-03 structural diff (base to draft) onto the new head, and a key conflict returns 409 `rebase_conflict`, so a stale draft never silently reverts someone else's change.
- Classification: pure `approvals.Classify(base, draft approvals.Doc) Classification{Widening bool; Reasons []Reason{Code, Path, Detail}; RequiredRole}` over the canonical doc. Allow and deny entries are compared as multisets keyed by an exported `DiffKey()` (the W-P1-PVER-03 diffKey, extended by W-P1-GPOL-01 with groups and users). Any added allow key is widening; there is no regex or wildcard containment analysis. The only allow narrowings are: an entry removed; an unscoped entry given groups or users, or a scoped entry's set reduced, on the same domain and port; a tighter rateLimit; a timeWindow added or narrowed. Removing or changing a deny entry is widening. Settings are compared by JSON path against a small allowlist of neutral or narrowing changes (logging.*, cacheTTLSeconds, dlp.enabled false to true, compliance.enabled false to true, advisory.enabled false to true). Every other path, including judge, llmProviders, secrets, explore, observability, mcp, agents and any field added later, is widening with code `settings.changed`. RequiredRole follows the W-P1-SSO-05 per-field table: admin for any settings field outside the editor set, else editor.
- Other targets: a Classifier and Applier pair is registered per target, so p4-mcp-registry adds `mcp_registry` without a schema change. W-P2-APPR-08 registers `blocked_users`, where BlockStore.Remove (W-P1-BLOCK-03) is always widening and becomes a pending change while adding a block stays immediate as the incident kill switch, and `agents`, where p2-agent-registry writes that create an agent, add an allowed group or allowed scope, add or replace a key, or re-enable an agent are widening and other agent edits (display name, removals, disable) apply directly. Lowering an agent's identity mode is a settings change (agents[].identity) and is held by the policy target.
- Independence and roles: a person is identified by (iss, sub). For an API key principal the owner identity from Principal.ActorSub() (W-P2-APIK-02) is used; approve, reject, emergency-apply and review are ScopeNone, so a key can create or edit a draft but never approve one. The approver must differ from the author, and with minApprovals > 1 approvers must be distinct. Break-glass sessions (auth_method breakglass, W-P1-OPS1-01) can never approve; they can only use emergency apply. Blocked principals already lose their sessions per W-P1-BLOCK-07. Roles are recomputed per request as in W-P1-SSO-05, and the approver must hold the draft's RequiredRole at approval time.
- Replay: new streaming `policyeval.Comparer` (`NewComparer(base, candidate config.Policy)`, `Add(analytics.Event)`, `Result() *CompareResult`) evaluates each event under both base and draft with the same stateless evaluator: rate limits and time windows stripped, and the W-P1-GPOL-05 subject used when the recorded identity status is valid. It reports changed_to_allow and changed_to_deny groups keyed by (domain, port, method) with count, affected users (email else sub, capped at 20), affected_users_total and anonymous_count, in a fixed sort order, with JSON tags and no URL, path, query or header. Recorded judge, DLP, block-list and rate-limit outcomes no longer show up as noise, because both sides are evaluated the same way. `policyeval.Evaluate` and `warden policy eval` are unchanged. Events come from a new `analytics.ReplayScanner` that FleetSQLiteStore implements on its read-only `ro` handle in pages of 5000 rows by id, selecting only the needed columns, so `/central/ingest` on the single read-write connection is never held for a whole scan. Other fleet stores fall back to one `GetEvents(EventFilter{Since, Limit})` call. One replay runs at a time per CP, bounded by replayTimeout, and replays left running by a CP restart are marked failed on startup.
- Approval needs evidence: an approve request carries the revision and doc_sha256 the reviewer saw, plus the `replay_id` of a done replay for that revision no older than replayMaxAge, or `acknowledgeNoReplay: true` when the latest replay is failed or unavailable (memory store with no events, empty window). Both are stored on the approval row and in the audit details. The UI states that replay covers allow and deny only, and that rate limits, time windows and settings are judged from the classification reasons.
- API, mounted under /dashboard/ so the W-P1-SSO-04 session and CSRF checks, the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table and the W-P1-AAUD-02 audit middleware apply unchanged, through a new `dashboard.ChangeDrafts` interface that only the CP sets (workers return 404): GET/POST /dashboard/api/changes, GET/PUT /dashboard/api/changes/{id}, GET .../{id}/diff, and POST .../{id}/submit|approve|reject|withdraw|rebase|replay, plus emergency-apply and review from W-P2-APPR-07. Each route has Action `change.draft.<verb>`, Target `change_draft` and Audited:true where it mutates. With approvals on, the existing policy, settings and llmProviders saves and rollback return 202 {draft_id, revision, state, widening, reasons} with a Location header when the change is held, or 200 {version} for a narrowing self-apply. The W-P1-PVER 409 and 428 If-Match rules still apply. API keys reach these routes through the W-P2-APIK-02 Scope column on the same table rows: GET routes policy:read; POST /dashboard/api/changes policy:draft; PUT, submit, withdraw, rebase and replay policy:write; approve, reject, emergency-apply and review ScopeNone. There is no policy:approve scope.
- Emergency path (W-P2-APPR-07): when allowEmergencyApply is true, a break-glass session may call `POST .../{id}/emergency-apply` with a reason of 10 to 512 characters. It publishes with an emergency Clearance, writes audit action `change.draft.emergency_apply`, logs at ERROR, publishes a critical integration.Finding with RuleID `approval_bypassed` and DedupKey `approval_bypassed:<draft id>`, and leaves the draft applied_unreviewed until an OIDC admin records `POST .../{id}/review`. With the flag off, or with Dex down and no break-glass, widening changes wait; narrowing changes and narrowing rollbacks still self-apply.
- Degraded modes: the worker hot path is untouched. Workers only see published versions and keep last-known-good while the CP is down. Drafts survive CP restarts in cpstate and are included in W-P1-OPS1-02 backups. With the IdP down, open sessions keep working and new logins wait. Expiry and replay windows use only the CP clock, and ordering uses version and revision integers. If admin audit is unhealthy, draft mutations return 503 per W-P1-AAUD-02.
- Observability: slog `change_draft_transition` with draft_id, revision, target, state_from, state_to, actor_sub, widening and reason codes, and slog `change_draft_replay` with draft_id, status, events, duration_ms and group counts. Doc content, settings values and credential values are never logged. Admin audit rows carry target_ref `draft:<id>@r<rev>` and details {base_version, applied_version, widening, reasons, replay_status, acknowledge_no_replay}; apply also writes the existing PVER `policy` row. An info Finding `policy_approval_requested` is published when a widening draft is submitted, so existing alert routes can notify reviewers. The CP has no metrics endpoint in P1, so pending count, oldest pending age, emergency applies and replay duration are recorded as hooks for W-P5-RETN-06.
- Dashboard: a Changes tab lists drafts by state and shows the W-P1-PVER-03 structural diff against base (credentials only as fingerprints), widening reasons and required role, replay status and age with the changed_to_allow and changed_to_deny tables, an acknowledge checkbox when the replay is unavailable, and approve, reject, withdraw and rebase controls. Every user-controlled string is rendered with textContent. Hidden buttons are a convenience only; the server enforces every check.

## Done when

On a CP with console.auth=oidc, --policy-store=versioned, --state-dir, admin audit enabled and console.approvals.enabled=true, an editor who adds an allow entry gets 202 with a pending draft whose reasons include allow.added, and the /policy ETag does not change. The same holds for a widening settings save (an llmProviders baseURL change, which also needs an admin approver), a rollback that drops a deny entry, `warden policy import` of a widening file, removing a block-list entry, lowering an agent's identity mode in settings (agents[].identity) and adding an allowed group to a registered agent. The author's own approval and any break-glass approval get 403. A second editor sees the structural diff, the reasons and a done replay comparing base and draft over fleet events, with affected users and no URLs; their approval publishes exactly one new version that workers receive within one long-poll cycle. Editing a draft voids its approvals, and approving after head moved yields needs_rebase. A narrowing change self-applies at once. A replay over 100k events does not stall /central/ingest. Every transition has a chained admin audit row, and with approvals disabled every P1 endpoint and /policy byte is unchanged.

### 1/9 · W-P2-APPR-01

**Add approvals config, draft store and state machine**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#101](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/101)

Add the CP-local `console.approvals` config block and the new internal/approvals package with the draft and approval tables, the Store and the state machine. Drafts hold the same redacted canonical doc_json as policy_versions and are applied only through the W-P1-PVER-02 publish path with expectedHead=base_version, so approvals can never skip validation, credential redaction or the policy audit row. Nothing is mounted on HTTP yet, and cmd/proxy refuses `enabled: true` until W-P2-APPR-06 gates every write path.

**Requirements**

- `console.approvals` is parsed by the W-P1-SSO-02 ConsoleConfig loader only from `--config` (`json:"-"`, never on policyWire or SettingsWire) with keys enabled (false), minApprovals (1, range 1..3), allowSelfApproveNarrowing (true), allowEmergencyApply (false), replayWindow (168h, 1h..720h), replayMaxEvents (100000, max 100000), replayTimeout (60s), replayMaxAge (24h), draftTTL (168h) and maxOpenDrafts (200); out-of-range values are validation errors.
- When enabled, startup fails with an error naming the missing item unless console.auth=oidc, `--policy-store=versioned`, `--state-dir` and `console.adminAudit.enabled=true`. A temporary guard refuses enabled with `approvals enforcement is not available in this build` until W-P2-APPR-06 removes it.
- Migration `approvals/0001` creates `change_drafts` and append-only `change_approvals` with the columns in the design, indexes on (state, target) and author_sub, and unique (draft_id, revision, approver_iss, approver_sub). It runs only when approvals are enabled.
- For the policy target, doc_json is the canonical doc {allowlist, denylist, settings}: secretAccessKey is replaced by its `sha256:<16 hex>` fingerprint before insert, blockedUsers is excluded, and doc_sha256 matches what policy_versions would compute for the same doc. YAML is never stored.
- Every transition is one transaction with `UPDATE ... WHERE id=? AND state=? AND revision=?`; 0 rows returns ErrStateChanged. Illegal transitions return ErrIllegalTransition. Update in draft or pending state creates revision n+1 and voids approvals for earlier revisions.
- Apply goes through a per-target `approvals.Applier`; the policy Applier lives in new internal/controlplane/approvals_apply.go over `s.publish` with expectedHead=base_version, source `approval`, and the draft author as author. internal/approvals never imports internal/controlplane. ErrConflict maps to ErrRebaseRequired and moves the draft to needs_rebase.
- Create returns ErrTooManyDrafts above maxOpenDrafts open drafts. A sweeper started from Server.Start moves draft, pending and needs_rebase drafts past expires_at to expired.
- Each transition logs `msg=change_draft_transition` with draft_id, revision, target, state_from, state_to and actor_sub; doc content and settings values are never logged.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/console.go (from W-P1-SSO-02): add `ConsoleApprovals` (new) to ConsoleConfig with defaults and validation; add the startup prerequisite checks and the temporary enabled guard in resolveConsole in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
2. Create internal/approvals (new): `Doc` with JSON tags allowlist, denylist and settings; `Author{Iss, Sub, Email, Kind}`; `Provenance`; `Draft`; the `State` enum and a pure `transition(from State, ev Event) (State, error)` table.
3. Add internal/approvals/store.go (new): `Store` interface and SQLite implementation on the cpstate *sql.DB with Create, Get, List(filter, cursor, limit), Update, Submit, RecordDecision, MarkApplied, MarkNeedsRebase, Withdraw and ExpireDue, plus the `approvals/0001` migration registered with cpstate.Open (W-P1-SSO-01).
4. Add `approvals.Service` (new) with `CreateDraft(ctx, target, doc, Author, Provenance, baseVersion)` and `Apply(ctx, id, revision)`, using the redaction helper exported from internal/controlplane/policystore.go (W-P1-PVER-01) through an injected func, and the `Applier` interface.
5. Add internal/controlplane/approvals_apply.go (new): the policy Applier over s.publish and the expiry sweeper goroutine, built in controlplane.New only when Config.Approvals is enabled.
6. Tests: internal/approvals/store_test.go (transition table, a CAS race under -race, revision bump voids approvals, no raw secretAccessKey in the DB file, expiry) and internal/controlplane/approvals_apply_test.go (stale base gives ErrRebaseRequired and no version; an applied draft creates one policy_versions row whose doc_sha256 equals the draft's); console_test.go for config validation.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given an applied draft, Submit, Update and Withdraw return ErrIllegalTransition and the row is unchanged; with 20 goroutines racing RecordDecision and Withdraw on one pending draft under -race, exactly one state change wins.
- [ ] Given a draft with base_version 3 while head is 4, Apply returns ErrRebaseRequired, head stays 4 and the draft is needs_rebase.
- [ ] Given a pending draft with base equal to head, Apply creates exactly one policy_versions row with source `approval` and the author's sub, and a second Apply returns ErrIllegalTransition without a new version.
- [ ] Given settings with secrets.secretAccessKey set, neither change_drafts.doc_json nor the DB file contains the raw value after CreateDraft.
- [ ] Given `console.approvals.enabled: true` with `console.auth: none`, the CP exits non-zero with an error naming console.auth; with approvals absent, /policy bytes and all P1 tests are unchanged.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/approvals ./internal/config -run 'TestDraftStore|TestDraftTransitions|TestDraftExpiry|TestConsoleApprovals'` and `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestDraftApplyPublish` pass.

### 2/9 · W-P2-APPR-02

**Implement widening-change classification**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#102](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/102)

Add a pure `approvals.Classify(base, draft Doc) Classification` that decides whether a policy doc change widens access or changes where credentials go, and which role must approve it. It works on the canonical doc the versioned store holds, so it only classifies fields that exist there: allow and deny entries with their groups and users, and SettingsWire. Anything it does not recognise counts as widening, so a new field can never slip through as narrowing.

**Requirements**

- Signature `Classify(base, draft approvals.Doc) Classification{Widening bool; Reasons []Reason{Code, Path, Detail string}; RequiredRole config.Role}`; no I/O, deterministic, reasons sorted by (Code, Path), and entry order in the input does not change the output.
- Allow and deny lists are compared as multisets keyed by an exported `DiffKey()` on config.AllowlistEntry and config.DenylistEntry (W-P1-PVER-03 diffKey renamed, including groups and users from W-P1-GPOL-01). Any added allow key is widening (`allow.added`); there is no regex or wildcard containment analysis. Removing or changing a deny entry is widening (`deny.removed`).
- Removed and added allow entries with the same domain and port are paired; the pair is narrowing only when an unscoped entry gains groups or users, a scoped entry's groups and users shrink, the rateLimit is tighter, or a timeWindow is added or narrowed. Otherwise it is widening with `allow.scope_widened`, `allow.rate_relaxed` or `allow.time_relaxed`. RateLimit and TimeWindow are parsed with the internal/policy rules, and an unparseable value is widening.
- Settings are compared by JSON path against an explicit table of neutral or narrowing changes: logging.*, cacheTTLSeconds, and dlp.enabled, compliance.enabled or advisory.enabled going from false to true. Every other added, removed or changed path is widening with code `settings.changed` and the path, including judge, llmProviders, secrets, explore, observability, mcp, agents and fields added later.
- RequiredRole is admin when any changed settings path is outside the W-P1-SSO-05 editor set (advisory, compliance, dlp, logging, agents, cacheTTLSeconds), otherwise editor. The set is shared with authz, so when W-P2-WBND-07 makes agents[].identity and identity.defaultMode admin-only, those changes need an admin approver.
- Reason Detail holds only domain, port and JSON path; credential paths show fingerprints and settings values are never included.
- Classify handles 5000 entries per side in under 50ms and runs only on draft create, update, rebase and apply, never on /policy.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/config/config.go: rename the W-P1-PVER-03 diffKey() to exported DiffKey() on AllowlistEntry and DenylistEntry and update internal/controlplane/policydiff.go callers.
2. Add internal/approvals/classify.go (new): multiset build by DiffKey, same-domain-and-port pairing, rate and time comparison, and the Reason codes.
3. Add internal/approvals/settings_rules.go (new): a JSON-path walker over config.SettingsWire marshalled to a generic map, the neutral and narrowing rule table, and the editor-field set shared with internal/controlplane/authz.go (move the set to internal/config so both import it).
4. Add internal/approvals/classify_test.go (new): one table case per reason code, narrowing-only cases, regex and wildcard additions, scoped-to-unscoped, an unknown settings path, and a fuzz test that Classify(x, x) is never widening; add BenchmarkClassify with 5000 entries.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Table test flags each of these with the expected reason code: allow entry added, exact domain replaced by `*.` wildcard, `~` regex changed, port changed, deny entry removed, groups removed from a scoped entry, rateLimit raised, timeWindow widened, dlp.enabled true to false, llmProviders entry added.
- [ ] A draft that only adds a deny entry, removes an allow entry, or adds groups to an unscoped entry gives Widening=false.
- [ ] A change to a settings path not in the rule table gives Widening=true with code `settings.changed` and that path; a change to llmProviders gives RequiredRole admin.
- [ ] Identical docs give Widening=false and no reasons, and shuffling entry order does not change the output.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/approvals -run 'TestClassify|FuzzClassify' -bench BenchmarkClassify` passes with the benchmark under 50ms per call.

### 3/9 · W-P2-APPR-03

**Replay fleet events against base and draft for each revision**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#103](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/103)

Add a two-policy replay that evaluates recent fleet events under both the base version and the draft and stores the differences on the draft revision. Comparing against the recorded decision would show judge, DLP, block-list and rate-limit outcomes as false changes, so both sides use the same stateless evaluator. Events are read in pages from the fleet store's read-only handle so a 100k-event replay never holds the ingest connection.

**Requirements**

- New `policyeval.NewComparer(base, candidate config.Policy) *Comparer` with `Add(analytics.Event)` and `Result() *CompareResult`: rate limits and time windows are stripped on both sides, the W-P1-GPOL-05 subject is used when the recorded identity status is valid, and Conditional and NoMatch count as deny. `Evaluate` and `warden policy eval` output stay unchanged.
- CompareResult has JSON tags: {events, agreed, anonymous_count, changed_to_allow[], changed_to_deny[]} with groups {domain, port, method, count, affected_users (email else sub, max 20), affected_users_total}, sorted by count desc then domain, port, method. No URL, path, query, header or group list is stored. MCP events are skipped.
- New optional interface `analytics.ReplayScanner{ScanReplayEvents(ctx, since time.Time, limit int, fn func(Event) error) error}` implemented by FleetSQLiteStore on the `ro` handle in pages of 5000 rows by descending id, selecting only ts, domain, port, protocol, method, decision and the W-P1-VRFY-06 user columns. Stores without it fall back to one GetEvents(EventFilter{Since, Limit}).
- Migration `approvals/0002` adds `draft_replays(id, draft_id, revision, base_version, status pending|running|done|failed|unavailable, window_from, window_to, events_scanned, truncated, result_json, error_code, started_at, finished_at)`.
- A replay is queued on submit and on every new revision; Submit never waits. One replay runs at a time per CP, bounded by replayTimeout; on timeout the replay is failed with error_code `timeout` and a late result is discarded. Zero events gives status unavailable. On startup, pending and running replays are marked failed with `interrupted`.
- `Service.Replay(ctx, id)` re-runs a replay at most once per minute per draft and returns ErrReplayBusy while the slot is in use. The route is added in W-P2-APPR-04.
- Each run logs `msg=change_draft_replay` with draft_id, status, events, duration_ms and group counts, and never domains or user identifiers.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add internal/policyeval/compare.go (new): Comparer, CompareResult and group types, reusing the per-event subject and scheme logic from eval.go (factor it into an unexported helper shared with Evaluate).
2. Add `ReplayScanner` (new) in internal/analytics/analytics.go and `ScanReplayEvents` (new) in internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite.go on s.ro, with page-by-id queries so the connection is released between pages.
3. Add internal/approvals/replay.go (new): the `approvals/0002` migration, a Replayer with a one-slot semaphore, the per-draft rate limit, the timeout and the startup recovery; base and draft docs are decoded to config.Policy through an injected decoder.
4. In internal/controlplane/approvals_apply.go wire the Replayer with s.central (using ReplayScanner when the store implements it) and the PVER-01 doc decoder.
5. Tests: internal/policyeval/compare_test.go, internal/analytics/fleet_sqlite_test.go for ScanReplayEvents, and internal/approvals/replay_test.go (timeout, busy, interrupted, no `url` key).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given events allowed to api.example.com:443, a draft that adds a deny for api.example.com has a changed_to_deny group {domain: api.example.com, port: 443, count: N} and no changed_to_allow groups.
- [ ] Given events recorded as denied by DLP or user_blocked to a domain that both base and draft allow, the result has no changed_to_allow groups for them.
- [ ] With replayTimeout set to 100ms and a scanner fake that blocks, Submit returns immediately and the replay becomes failed with `timeout` within 200ms.
- [ ] While a 100k-event ScanReplayEvents runs on a file-backed FleetSQLiteStore, a concurrent StoreAggregatedEvent completes in under 100ms.
- [ ] The stored result_json for events whose URLs have paths and queries contains no `url` key, no `/` path segment and no `?`.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/policyeval -run TestCompare` and `go test -race ./internal/analytics ./internal/approvals -run 'TestScanReplayEvents|TestReplay'` pass.

### 4/9 · W-P2-APPR-04

**Add the change draft API with the two-person rule**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#104](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/104)

Mount the draft routes under /dashboard/api/changes so the existing session, CSRF, role table and admin audit middleware cover them, and enforce the two-person rule on approve. An approval is bound to the revision, doc_sha256 and replay the reviewer saw, and the final approval applies the draft in the same request so there is no gap between approval and publish. Rerouting the existing write paths is W-P2-APPR-06.

**Requirements**

- New `dashboard.ChangeDrafts` interface and setter, set only on the CP (workers return 404), with routes: GET /dashboard/api/changes?target=&state=&cursor=&limit= and GET .../{id} and GET .../{id}/diff (viewer); POST /dashboard/api/changes and PUT .../{id} with If-Match `"r<rev>"` (editor, author only for PUT); POST .../{id}/submit, withdraw and rebase (author); POST .../{id}/approve and reject (editor or the draft's RequiredRole); POST .../{id}/replay (editor). Every route is in dashboard.Routes() and the W-P1-SSO-05 authz table with Action `change.draft.<verb>`, Target `change_draft` and Audited:true on mutations, and the W-P2-APIK-02 Scope (policy:read for GET, policy:draft for create, policy:write for PUT, submit, withdraw, rebase and replay, ScopeNone for approve and reject), set by whichever of the two tickets lands second.
- GET .../{id}/diff returns the W-P1-PVER-03 structural diff of the current revision against base_version, with credential paths only as fingerprints.
- Approve body {revision, doc_sha256, replay_id | acknowledgeNoReplay, comment<=1024}. It is refused with 409 `revision_changed` when revision or doc_sha256 differ from the draft, and with 409 `replay_required` unless replay_id names a done replay for that revision no older than replayMaxAge, or acknowledgeNoReplay is true and the latest replay is failed or unavailable.
- Two-person rule: the approver's identity from Principal.ActorSub() (the owner for API-key principals, W-P2-APIK-02) must differ from the author's (403 `self_approval_forbidden`); auth_method breakglass can never approve (403 `breakglass_cannot_approve`); the approver must hold RequiredRole when the request runs (403 `role_required` with the fields). With minApprovals > 1 approvers must be distinct.
- When the last required approval arrives, the same request re-runs Classify against the live head and applies; 200 {state: applied, version}, 409 `rebase_required` {head} when head moved (draft becomes needs_rebase), 422 with the loader error when validation fails (draft stays pending). Submit of a narrowing draft applies at once with decision `self` when allowSelfApproveNarrowing is true.
- Rebase applies the PVER-03 diff (base to draft) onto head as revision n+1 and returns 409 `rebase_conflict` when a key changed on both sides.
- A `change_draft` StateHasher (`<id>:<revision>:<state>:<doc_sha256>`) is registered with W-P1-AAUD-02, handlers call adminaudit.Annotate with target_ref `draft:<id>@r<rev>` and details {base_version, applied_version, widening, reasons, replay_status, acknowledge_no_replay}, and never doc content. Submit of a widening draft publishes an info Finding `policy_approval_requested` (DedupKey per draft).
- Request bodies are capped at 1 MiB and comments have control characters stripped; unknown id 404, illegal transition 409 `illegal_transition`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add internal/dashboard/dashboard_changes.go (new): the ChangeDrafts interface, SetChangeDrafts setter and handlers, registered from the Routes() list.
2. Add the routes with Action, Target and Audited to the internal/controlplane/authz.go table and extend the route-coverage test.
3. Add `Service.Approve`, `Reject`, `Withdraw`, `Rebase` and `Submit` self-apply logic in internal/approvals/service.go (new), taking the actor from dashboard PrincipalFrom(ctx) mapped to approvals.Author.
4. Add internal/controlplane/approvals_http.go (new): the adapter implementing dashboard.ChangeDrafts over approvals.Service, the PVER-03 DiffDocs call for /diff and rebase, the change_draft StateHasher and the Finding publish through Server.publishFinding (W-P1-OPS1-01).
5. Tests in internal/controlplane/approvals_api_test.go (new) with editor sessions u1 and u2, a viewer, an admin and a break-glass session created through SessionStore.Create.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given u1's pending widening draft, u1's POST .../approve returns 403 `self_approval_forbidden` and writes an admin_audit row with outcome denied; a break-glass session's approve returns 403 `breakglass_cannot_approve`.
- [ ] Given u2 with a done replay_id, POST .../approve returns 200 with version=head+1, a worker long-polling /policy receives the new ETag within one wait, and admin audit holds change.draft.create, change.draft.submit, change.draft.approve and the PVER policy row in order.
- [ ] Given an approval sent with an older revision after u1 PUT a new revision, the response is 409 `revision_changed` and no version is created.
- [ ] Given a widening draft that adds an llmProviders entry, u2's approve returns 403 `role_required` naming llmProviders and an admin's approve succeeds.
- [ ] Given head moved after submit, approve returns 409 `rebase_required`; rebase creates revision 2 and its earlier approvals are void.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestChangeDraftAPI|TestTwoPersonRule|TestAuthzMatrix|TestAdminAuditCoverage'` passes.

**Depends on:** [`W-P2-APPR-01`](policy-approvals.md#19--w-p2-appr-01) Add approvals config, draft store and state machine; [`W-P2-APPR-02`](policy-approvals.md#29--w-p2-appr-02) Implement widening-change classification; [`W-P2-APPR-03`](policy-approvals.md#39--w-p2-appr-03) Replay fleet events against base and draft for each revision; [`W-P1-SSO-05`](console-sso-rbac.md#58--w-p1-sso-05) Enforce role checks on every dashboard route; [`W-P1-AAUD-02`](admin-audit-log.md#24--w-p1-aaud-02) Record CP admin mutations and logins through audit middleware; [`W-P1-PVER-03`](policy-versioning.md#36--w-p1-pver-03) Add policy history, structural diff and rollback APIs; [`W-P1-OPS1-01`](ops-hardening.md#14--w-p1-ops1-01) Add break-glass local admin with alerting and audit

### 5/9 · W-P2-APPR-05

**Add the Changes tab with structural diff and replay view**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#105](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/105)

Add a Changes tab to the dashboard where reviewers see each draft's structural diff, widening reasons, required role and replay result before they approve. It reuses the W-P1-PVER-04 diff renderer so credentials appear only as fingerprints, and it handles the 202 response that policy, settings and llmProviders saves return when a change is held. The server stays the only enforcement point; hidden buttons are a convenience.

**Requirements**

- The Changes tab shows only when GET /dashboard/api/setup reports approvals enabled. It lists drafts by state with target, author, source, base version, revision, age, widening badge, required role and replay status, and loads more with a cursor.
- The detail view renders GET .../{id}/diff with the PVER-04 renderer (no client-side YAML or text diff), the reason codes, and the changed_to_allow and changed_to_deny tables with affected users, event count, window_from and a truncated banner. It states that replay covers allow and deny only.
- Approve sends revision, doc_sha256 and replay_id. When the replay is failed or unavailable, an acknowledge checkbox must be ticked to send acknowledgeNoReplay. A pending replay polls every 2s up to replayTimeout and then offers re-run.
- Controls use data-min-role; approve is hidden for the author and for break-glass sessions per /auth/me, and controls for states needs_rebase, expired and applied_unreviewed show the matching action or a read-only badge.
- Policy, settings and llmProviders save flows handle 202 by showing `submitted for review` with a link to the draft, and do not report the change as saved.
- All writes use the W-P1-SSO-04 api() wrapper with X-Warden-CSRF and If-Match; author, message, comment, domain, user and reason strings are set only with textContent.

**Implementation plan**

1. internal/dashboard/index.html: add the Changes tab container, list view, detail view and polling logic, reusing the PVER-04 diff renderer function.
2. internal/dashboard/index.html: update the policy, settings and llmProviders save handlers for the 202 response.
3. Add an `approvalsEnabled` field to the GET /dashboard/api/setup response in internal/dashboard (set through the ChangeDrafts seam).
4. Tests: internal/dashboard/changes_tab_test.go (new) with TestChangesTab, TestChangesTabTextContent and TestPolicySaveDraft.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] The served HTML contains the Changes container, fetches `/dashboard/api/changes`, renders the diff via the PVER-04 renderer and posts approve with revision, doc_sha256 and replay_id.
- [ ] A template test asserts that author, message, comment, domain, user and reason fields are assigned only through textContent and never innerHTML.
- [ ] A save that returns 202 shows a link to the draft and no `saved` message.
- [ ] With approvals disabled, GET /dashboard/ HTML behaves as in P1 and the Changes tab is not shown.
- [ ] `go test ./internal/dashboard -run 'TestChangesTab|TestChangesTabTextContent|TestPolicySaveDraft'` passes.

### 6/9 · W-P2-APPR-06

**Gate every versioned write path through one clearance check**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#259](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/259)

Make `Server.publish` require an `approvals.Clearance` that only `approvals.Gate` can mint, so no write path can publish a widening change without a draft. With approvals enabled, WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteLLMProviders, the rollback route and `warden policy import` create drafts and return 202 when the change is widening, and apply at once when it is narrowing. This removes the temporary startup guard from W-P2-APPR-01.

**Requirements**

- `approvals.Clearance` has unexported fields and `Server.publish` returns ErrNotCleared for the zero value. `Gate.Clear(ctx, change)` mints one when approvals are disabled, for a narrowing change when allowSelfApproveNarrowing is true, for an applied draft, and for `system:import`; otherwise it returns ErrApprovalRequired. Emergency clearance is added in W-P2-APPR-07.
- With approvals enabled, a widening save on POST/PUT /dashboard/api/policy, /dashboard/api/settings or the llmproviders route creates and submits a draft (source console, base_version from If-Match) and returns 202 {draft_id, revision, state, widening, reasons} with a Location header; a narrowing save returns 200 {version}. Stale If-Match still returns 409 `policy_conflict` and a missing one 428.
- Field-level role checks from W-P1-SSO-05 still run at save time; the held draft's RequiredRole is enforced again at approve time.
- POST /dashboard/api/policy/versions/{v}/rollback with approvals enabled creates a draft whose doc is version v (source rollback), classified against head; a narrowing rollback applies at once.
- `warden policy import` with approvals enabled creates a pending draft authored `cli:<os user>` (author_kind cli, source cli) instead of a version, prints the draft id and writes an admin audit row; the CP queues its replay on the next sweep. The CLI cannot approve or apply. It detects approvals through a new single-row `approvals_meta` table the CP writes at startup.
- With approvals disabled, every write path, status code and /policy byte is unchanged and the existing P1 tests pass unmodified apart from the publish call sites.
- docs/control-plane.md lists which writes are gated (policy, settings, llmProviders, rollback, CLI import) and which are not (integrations, detection, console).

**Implementation plan**

1. Add internal/approvals/gate.go (new): Clearance, Gate, Change{Target, Base, Draft Doc, Author, Source} and Clear.
2. internal/controlplane/controlplane.go: change Server.publish (W-P1-PVER-02) to take a Clearance; update WritePolicy, WriteSettings, WriteLLMProviders (llmproviders_write.go), importInitialVersion (policystore.go) and the policy Applier to obtain one from s.gate.
3. On ErrApprovalRequired in those writers, call approvals.Service.CreateDraft and Submit and return a typed `HeldForApproval` result; map it to 202 in the dashboard handlers in internal/dashboard/dashboard.go and dashboard_llmproviders.go.
4. internal/controlplane/policyhistory.go: route Rollback through the Gate the same way.
5. cmd/proxy/policy_import.go (W-P1-PVER-06): read approvals_meta and create a draft through approvals.Store when enabled; remove the temporary guard in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
6. Tests: internal/controlplane/approvals_writepaths_test.go (new) and cmd/proxy/policy_import_test.go cases; update docs/control-plane.md.

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given approvals enabled and head v4, a settings save that sets dlp.enabled false returns 202 with a widening draft and head stays 4; a save that adds a deny entry returns 200 with version 5.
- [ ] Given approvals enabled, rollback to v2 where v2 lacks a deny entry present in v4 returns 202 with reason deny.removed and head stays 4.
- [ ] Given approvals enabled, `warden policy import --file wider.yaml` creates one pending draft and one admin_audit row with actor `cli:<user>`, and head is unchanged.
- [ ] Calling Server.publish with the zero `approvals.Clearance{}` returns ErrNotCleared and creates no version.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestApprovalsWritePaths|TestRollbackAsDraft|TestPublishRequiresClearance'` and `go test ./cmd/proxy -run TestPolicyImportApprovals` pass, and `go test ./...` passes with approvals disabled.

### 7/9 · W-P2-APPR-07

**Add audited break-glass emergency apply with post-hoc review**

Type **feature** · Size **S** · Issue [#260](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/260)

When Dex is down nobody can log in to approve, so add an opt-in emergency apply that only a break-glass session can use. It publishes a pending widening draft, raises a critical Finding and leaves the draft applied_unreviewed until an OIDC admin records a review. It is off unless `console.approvals.allowEmergencyApply` is true.

**Requirements**

- `POST /dashboard/api/changes/{id}/emergency-apply` {reason 10..512 chars} is allowed only for auth_method breakglass (W-P1-OPS1-01) and only when allowEmergencyApply is true; otherwise 403 `emergency_apply_disabled` or `breakglass_required`. It works on pending and needs_rebase drafts and still uses expectedHead (409 on conflict).
- The Gate mints an emergency Clearance for this call only. The draft moves to applied_unreviewed, and a change_approvals row with decision `emergency` records the reason.
- Each emergency apply writes admin audit action `change.draft.emergency_apply`, logs one ERROR line `msg=approval_bypassed` with draft_id and actor_sub, and publishes a critical integration.Finding with RuleID `approval_bypassed` and DedupKey `approval_bypassed:<draft id>`. The reason text is not logged.
- `POST .../{id}/review` {comment} by an OIDC admin moves applied_unreviewed to applied with decision `post_review`; break-glass sessions cannot review.
- A startup WARN is logged when allowEmergencyApply is true but break-glass is disabled or no alert route matches `approval_bypassed`.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add the emergency Clearance and `Service.EmergencyApply` and `Service.Review` in internal/approvals/gate.go and service.go.
2. Add the two routes to internal/dashboard/dashboard_changes.go and the authz table (emergency-apply admin plus breakglass check in the handler, review admin), both Audited:true.
3. Publish the Finding through Server.publishFinding in internal/controlplane/approvals_http.go and add the startup WARN in cmd/proxy/controlplane.go.
4. Tests in internal/controlplane/approvals_emergency_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] With allowEmergencyApply false, a break-glass emergency-apply returns 403 and head is unchanged.
- [ ] With it true, an OIDC admin's emergency-apply returns 403 `breakglass_required`, and a break-glass call with a 20-character reason publishes head+1, sets applied_unreviewed, writes one change.draft.emergency_apply row and one `approval_bypassed` Finding.
- [ ] An OIDC admin's review moves the draft to applied; a break-glass review returns 403.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run TestEmergencyApply` passes.

### 8/9 · W-P2-APPR-08

**Hold block-list removals and widening agent edits for approval**

Type **feature** · Size **M** · Issue [#261](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/261)

Unblocking a user and loosening an agent widen access without touching the policy doc, so register `blocked_users` and `agents` as draft targets with their own Classifier and Applier. Adding a block stays immediate because it is the incident kill switch. This also proves the target-generic design that p4-mcp-registry will reuse.

**Requirements**

- With approvals enabled, DELETE /dashboard/api/blocked-users/{id} (W-P1-BLOCK-03) creates a pending `blocked_users` draft (target_ref the entry id, doc the entry without the reason text) and returns 202; POST to add a block still applies at once. Approval needs a second admin, and the Applier calls BlockStore.Remove with the approver recorded.
- With approvals enabled, agent registry writes (W-P2-AREG-02 Store.Create, Update and SetStatus) that create an agent, add an allowed group or allowed scope, add or replace a key, or re-enable an agent create a pending `agents` draft and return 202; other agent edits (display name, removals, disable) apply directly. A held update keeps the If-Match revision as its base. JWK material is stored only as kid and thumbprint in the draft.
- The two-person rule, evidence rule (acknowledgeNoReplay, since replay does not apply), audit details and Findings from W-P2-APPR-04 apply unchanged to these targets.
- The Applier re-reads current state and returns ErrRebaseRequired when the entry or agent changed since the draft was created.
- With approvals disabled, block-list and agent registry behaviour is unchanged.

**Implementation plan**

1. Add internal/approvals/targets.go (new): the Classifier and Applier registry keyed by target.
2. Add internal/controlplane/approvals_blocklist.go (new): Classifier (removal always widening) and Applier over BlockStore; change the DELETE handler wiring to go through the Gate.
3. Add internal/controlplane/approvals_agents.go (new): Classifier comparing old and new agentreg.Agent fields, and Applier over agentreg.Store; route the AREG-02 write handlers through the Gate.
4. Tests in internal/controlplane/approvals_targets_test.go (new).

**Acceptance criteria**

- [ ] Given approvals enabled, deleting a block entry returns 202, the served /policy still lists the user, and a second admin's approval removes it and wakes long-poll waiters.
- [ ] Given approvals enabled, adding a block entry returns 201 and the user is denied at once.
- [ ] Given approvals enabled, adding an allowed group to an agent returns 202 and the served wire is unchanged until a second approval; changing its display name applies directly.
- [ ] `go test -race ./internal/controlplane -run 'TestApprovalsBlockList|TestApprovalsAgents'` passes.

### 9/9 · W-P2-APPR-09

**Add approvals end-to-end test and operator docs**

Type **test** · Size **S** · Issue [#262](https://github.com/ethosagent/warden/issues/262)

Prove the done_when end to end with an in-process CP, two editor sessions and a long-polling worker, and document the approvals flow for operators. The test covers the policy path, a held settings save, a rollback, and the admin audit chain.

**Requirements**

- A test in internal/controlplane runs a CP with versioned store, admin audit and approvals enabled, editor sessions u1 and u2, and a fake worker long-polling /policy.

- A narrowing change applies at once, and a held llmProviders change needs an admin approver.
- `warden control-plane admin-audit verify --state-dir <dir>` (W-P1-AAUD-04) over the test state dir reports ok with the create, submit, approve and policy rows in order.
- New docs/approvals.md covers config keys, prerequisites, the state machine, what is and is not gated, the 202 contract, emergency apply and the replay limits; docs/control-plane.md links to it and the production-readiness checklist gains a row.
